name: Keap
summary: CRM, sales and marketing automation built for small businesses. Capture leads, automate follow-up and manage your pipeline in one place.
best_for: service-based small businesses, coaches and solopreneurs who want CRM, email, payments and automation in one tool, and will invest the time to learn it
skip_if: you're price-sensitive, want a modern UI, or only need simple email: the cost and learning curve bite
honest_knock: Cost is the big one (56% of reviewers flag it), the interface feels dated, and there's a real 2–4 week learning curve on the automation builder. Billing and cancellation complaints are common: their own terms carry a $299 early termination fee on an annual contract and require ten days' phone notice, and email design is thinner than dedicated email tools.

pricing.entry_price_terms: the whole platform · billed monthly for 2 users and 1,500 contacts
pricing.notes: Starting at $320 a month billed monthly for the whole platform, with no feature-based tiers and no free plan (re-read 21 and 24 November 2026 from the plan data behind the calculator on keap.com/pricing; on 24 September 2026 the same minimum was $299). That $320 is what the calculator quotes for its own minimum: 2 users and 1,500 contacts. The contact steps did not move, so raising only the contact count now gives $356 at 2,500, $470 at 5,000, $560 at 10,000 and $740 at 25,000, and users beyond the first two are $39 a month each. The same price card carries an annual line, 'Billed at $3,195 /year', for the base configuration. Keap also requires paid implementation services (strategy consulting, data import and migration), quoted separately before you go live. Text marketing is bundled at Tier 1 (500 messages and 100 voice minutes) and steps to $24, $39, $79, $139 and $279 a month above that, with overages at $0.015 a message and $0.01 a voice minute; it is US-only. Cancelling an annual contract before its term ends carries a $299 early termination fee, and cancellation must be started by phone at least ten days before the next invoice date. Keap has been acquired by Thryv; its own pages now route training to Thryv Academy.
